shape.text: Adobe's archived instructions have the developer generate the private key locally with an OpenSSL command that requests a 2048-bit RSA key and writes it to a file named private.key.
Adobe's pages state an encoding, header label or length for the contents of the private key file.

unresolved.reason: The pages read name the file and the generator command but state no encoding, header label or length for the key file.

issuance.text: Adobe's archived instructions have the developer upload the public certificate when creating the integration, and the private key signs a JWT with RS256 that is sent as the jwt_token parameter to obtain an access token, with no parameter that carries the private key itself.

lifecycle.text: Adobe states it announced the deprecation of Service Account (JWT) credentials on May 1, 2023 and that after June 3, 2024 new ones cannot be created.
Archived captures of one Adobe migration page state end-of-life dates of Jan 1, 2025, then Jan 27, 2025, then Jun 30, 2025, so the stated dates are announcements that changed.

Adobe's current pages state that Service Account (JWT) credentials reached end of life on June 30, 2025 and will be converted to OAuth Server-to-Server credentials when certificates expire or on March 1, 2026, whichever is earlier.
Adobe states the date on which a given Service Account (JWT) exchange last succeeded.

unresolved.reason: The pages state announcement, creation-stop, end-of-life and conversion dates but no per-credential last-success date, and no exchange was attempted.

collisions.text: The retired private key carries an Adobe-specific marker that distinguishes it from other RSA private keys.

unresolved.reason: The key is generated by a general-purpose tool and the pages read state no Adobe-specific marker, so no distinguishing shape is established.
